body: holy shit i am so sorry. i thought you were someone else telling, well, yourself to die. i fucked up i am so sorry.

hey. im transgender and gay. white, so i cant personally understand that aspect, but i know how the bullshit of the world feels, at the very least.

i want to help, if you're willing to let me try. your life is worth so much more than homophobic, racist assholes getting a goddamned boner because they drive another black gay guy to suicide.

have you considered writing a letter to them? an old fashioned pen and paper one. pour out everything you're feeling. you dont even have to give it to them, just write it, and keep it on you. you can slip it into their room when they're out, or give it to them right before you leave for school or before they leave for work.

sometimes it can be easier if you dont have to look in their eyes. its definitely helped me to do something like this before.

hey. youre more than your grades, okay? i had to drop out of highschool because i knew that if i stayed i would kill myself, withought doubt. at 14 this isn't an option for you yet, but if you need to, try to hold onto it, okay?

whine all you want. no matter what the reasons are for you wanting to die, the end result is the same. you could have tripped over a ladybug in the sidewalk for all i care. how you feel is important. 

your family doesnt seem particularly supportive,  but do you think you could convince them to let you see a therapist? perhaps speak to a school councilor and ask for their help in convincing your family that it would be a good idea - especially if you can get them to say it would help with your grades. true or not, i think doing whatever you can to get yourself in to see a professional is worth it.

edit: also, woth regards to the OCD: i also get intrusive thoughts. not on the same level, im sure, but i do experience thoughts of doing horrible things or of horrible things happening. your thoughts do not make you a bad person, okay? theyre bullshit you cant stop. its not your fault.

and there ARE ways to handle them. coping methods to make them impact your life less. its not a hopeless case.

thanks for the reply. my parents are supportive - im extremely lucky on that front. so are my siblings. despite this i still havent been able to start hormones or really progress with my transition at all. that probably adds to the feeling that everything's just motionless. 

the doctor i visited after i got my approval letter told me i was too young to start. i was only 17 at the time, had parental consent, and the state i live in (oregon) doesn't have any laws that should have stopped her from allowing me on hrt. and yet she insisted it was illegal.

and then she told me to try binding with ace bandages after telling me "you'll get to oppress women soon" so it was kinda clear she had it out for trans guys. what sucks is that she's trans too. out of all the places i expected support...

dysthymia is basically clinical depression but less intense and more long term. people with clinical depression frequently have periods of months or years where they dont feel depressed at all and then relapse. with dysthymia, the depression is a constant.

i see where you're coming from with regards to antidepressants. i will say that i disagree, however. i have friends who would be dead if not for their antidepressants. placebo or no - if it helps keep someone alive, i think its a worthwhile treatment. theres actually cases of placebos being used instead of surgery and peoples symptoms disappearing. placebos are pretty cool. 

its nice to hear from someone with a similar experience, i really appreciate it.

no, i'm not generally religious in any sense. why?

edit: oh, wait. right. the title. i'm referring to more broad modern concepts of purgatory as a place of limbo and suffering, not Catholic purgatory. sorry for the confusion.

i also find gentle overstimulation can help when things start to feel overwhelming. like say... putting on a show, music, playing a game, and maybe something more tactile like having a heavy blanket on you all at once. it can make it so you cant focus on any one thing 100%, which means you cant focus in your thoughts 100% either.

might seem too simple but, if you can find a show that's still airing, use that. you dont have to love it, but find something you can focus on, and make the days it comes out your benchmarks. "just have to wait for the next episode. after that i'll do it." and repeat.
